why: Shaodian is the Yellow Emperor's father (Shiji, Basic Annals of the Five Emperors; Guoyu), not his son; the son link (with Nüwa) closed an ancestor loop. Emma, 2026-10-29: "for some reason Shaodian is listed as his son somewhere. But Shaodian is his father."
The same reversed link in the MyHeritage copy of the line: (Shǎo Diǎn) as the son of Xuanyuan and Nvwa. Emma, 2026-10-29, as above

Suppone I (b. 760) as a son of Mauringo of Spoleto (b. 795): reversed; Mauringo is Suppo's son. Dates, under Emma's 2026-10-29 rule for the loops ("the people in these loops typically have dates ... we can pretty easily just cut out the wrong merge")
Ceionius Rufius Volusianus Lampadius (b. 315) as a son of Ceionius Rufius Albinus (b. 343): the parent is born after the child; the Albinus born 343 is Lampadius's son. Dates, as above
Henry I, Count of Stade (b. 929) as a son of Lothar II von Stade (b. 950): the parent is born after the child. Dates, as above
Geoffroi I de Joigny (b. 982) as a son of Mainfraida (b. 1000): the parent is born after the child. Dates, as above
Olof Jonsson (b. 1420) as a son of Jon Olofsson (b. 1460): the parent is born after the child; Jon Olofsson is Olof's son. Dates, as above
Arne Holar as a son of Halldor Arnesson (b. 1300): Arnesson is "Arne's son"; the link is reversed. Name and dates, as above
Gaius Caecilius (b. 400 BC) as a son of a late Lucius Caecilius Metellus (son of one born c. 130 BC): an ancestor of the Metelli listed under a descendant. Dates, as above

Velazco de Pampelune (b. 710) as a son of Galindo "Belascotenes" ("son of Velasco"), who is himself the father of Velasco Galindez (b. 730): reversed. Name and dates, as above
Hawise, Duchess of Brittany (Alan IV's mother, wife of Hoel II, daughter of Alan III) as a daughter of Alan IV: his daughter Hawise is a separate record in his other family. Dates, as above
Engenulf de l'Aigle (b. ABT 1009) as a son of Richeveride (b. ABT 1009), his wife (their son Richard b. 1039): a stray one-parent family. Dates, as above
Richeveride (b. ABT 1009) as a daughter of Engenulf de l'Aigle, her husband: a stray one-parent family. Dates, as above
Conrad I of Swabia (b. ABT 925) as a son of Judith of Öhningen, who is his daughter (wife of Adalbert of Metz); his parents Udo I and Cunégonde stay. Dates and records, as above
